content.text: Sharding distributes data across multiple machines (shards). MongoDB routes queries to the correct shard using a shard key.

content.definition: The field (or fields) MongoDB uses to distribute documents across shards. Choose it carefully — it cannot be changed.

content.text: Hashed shard keys give even distribution. Range shard keys allow efficient range queries but risk hotspots.

questions.question: What is a hotspot in a sharded cluster?
options: A shard receiving disproportionately more writes than others
questions.explanation: A hotspot occurs when one shard receives most of the traffic, defeating the purpose of sharding.

faq.a: Only shard when a single replica set can no longer handle your data volume or write throughput. Sharding adds operational complexity.

examples: Sharding user events by hashed userId
